- `tests/test_views/test_auction_view_player_listing.py` (NEW — PREVIEW shows "List a Lot" button when player tier >= regular at Stellaris; button absent when tier < regular OR venue_id != "stellaris"; "Active Listings" subsection renders one row per listing in `auction_state.active_listings`; BID_WINDOW for a player-seller lot suppresses raise/hold/fold buttons and renders the "Your lot — watching" banner; LOT_RESOLUTION for a player-seller lot displays the sold/withdrawn message variant; POST_SESSION renders Sable's `player_listing_post_session` line if a player lot resolved this session AND Sable is on crew; voice-template extension keys (`consigned_lot_lines`, `player_listing_post_session`) load through the existing data-loader path)
- `tests/test_scenarios/test_scenario_player_listing.py` (NEW — full scenario: regular-tier Stellaris player → Sell Lot view → consign 1 cargo commodity (declared appraisal 8,000, reserve 0.70) → fee deducted, item removed, listing appended → next scheduled Stellaris session → player lot is first lot in session → AI buyers bid (deterministic with locked seed) → lot sells at hammer price above reserve → player credited at hammer price → first-sale journal entry fires → `auction_first_sale` flag set → `auction_listings_sold` increments to 1 → second scenario branch: same player consigns a second lot but sets reserve at 0.95 (above any AI ceiling per locked seed) → AI bids stop below reserve → withdrawn → item returned to inventory → fee NOT refunded → `auction_first_listing_withdrawn` flag set; assert all callbacks fire in correct order; assert no UI element leaks; assert achievement stub `auction_seller` registered)
- `tests/test_data_integrity/test_player_listing_voice.py` (NEW — Writing Bible scan over the new `consigned_lot_lines` + `player_listing_post_session` voice templates AND the 3 new journal entries AND the SellLotView UI strings; voice-distinctness assertion that `consigned_lot_lines` matches Velo's ceremonial register (NOT Floor Manager terse register) so the consigned-lot announcement reads as a Stellaris event; Sable's `player_listing_post_session` reads must not collapse into universal-wisdom register — copy a paired example from `aurelia_voice_examples.md` if drafting feels generic)

**Deliverables.**
- **`_PlayerListing` model** — frozen dataclass in `spacegame/models/bidding.py` carrying the listing-specific fields the player chose (item kind, item id, quantity, declared appraisal, reserve_pct, listing fee paid, listed_on_day, headline, description, category). `to_auction_lot()` produces an `AuctionLot` with `seller_id="player"`, `venue="stellaris"`, `is_headliner=False`, `season_tag=None`, `faction_gate=None`, `rep_tier_required="regular"` (the listing tier-gate is mirrored on the resulting lot for symmetry), `recently_seen_count=0`, `contraband=False` (locked decision §B5.5: the SA-B5 sprint ships only non-contraband listings), `source_module_id=None`, `base_appraisal=declared_appraisal`. Backwards-compatible serialization via `data.get(field, default)` per §8.3.
- **AuctionState player-listing extension** — 3 new fields (`active_listings`, `listing_history`, plus 3 counters `auction_listings_sold`, `auction_listings_attempted`, `auction_listing_fees_paid`); 3 new methods (`create_listing`, `cancel_listing`, `eligible_listings_for_session`); `_resolve_lot` extended so when `lot.seller_id == "player"`, the sale price credits the player (caller-side via the engine callback), the listing dict moves to `listing_history` with the resolution outcome, and `auction_listings_sold` increments only on `sold=True`. All save/load defaults safe; old saves load cleanly.
- **`AuctionLot.seller_id` field** — `Optional[str] = None`; `to_dict` emits the field only when non-None so SA-B3/B4 catalog files stay byte-identical and the data-loader's `from_dict` reads the field as `None` for catalog lots.
- **SellLotView** — net-new view at `spacegame/views/sell_lot_view.py`. Two-pane layout (item-selection left, listing form right), tier-locked banner for sub-regular players, empty-state from the `consigned_lot_lines.empty_inventory` voice key, FirstTimeTipOverlay on first entry, fee-preview live-updates with the declared-appraisal field, reserve-pct slider clamped to [0.50, 0.95], Confirm button gated on (tier >= regular) AND (active_listings count < `MAX_ACTIVE_LISTINGS=3`) AND (player credits >= computed listing fee) AND (declared appraisal > 0) AND (reserve_pct in valid range). On confirm, calls `auction_state.create_listing(...)` and routes back to `GameState.AUCTION`. Standard BaseView lifecycle; UI elements destroyed in `_destroy_ui`.
- **Listing economics constants** — `LISTING_FEE_RATE = 0.05` (5% of declared appraisal), `LISTING_FEE_FLOOR = 100` (minimum fee in credits), `LISTING_RESERVE_PCT_MIN = 0.50`, `LISTING_RESERVE_PCT_MAX = 0.95`, `LISTING_RESERVE_PCT_DEFAULT = 0.70`, `MAX_ACTIVE_LISTINGS = 3`, `LISTING_TIER_REQUIRED = "regular"`. All in `spacegame/config.py`. SA-B6 may tune.
- **Eligibility rules** — listable items: (a) any commodity in `player.ship.current_cargo` (quantity > 0), (b) any ship part in `player.parts_inventory` (count > 0). NOT listable: `unlocked_modules` (boss-drop legendary set per §11.10), `ground_equipment` (ground-side, not ship-side), `salvage_hold_manager` contents (per-system buffer, must transfer to cargo first), installed equipment on the ship (player must un-equip before listing). Eligibility check happens both in SellLotView's filtering and in `create_listing` validation. Locked decision §B5.4.
- **AuctionView player-seller integration** — PREVIEW shows a "List a Lot" button (Stellaris-only, regular+ tier); "Active Listings" subsection lists current consignments. BID_WINDOW special-cases player-seller lots: bid action buttons hidden, "Your lot — watching" banner rendered, AI bidders behave normally. LOT_RESOLUTION renders sold/withdrawn message variants for player lots. POST_SESSION renders Sable's `player_listing_post_session` line when applicable.
- **Engine wiring (`_prepare_stellaris_session` extension + new callbacks)** — Before persona attendance, the prepare helper calls `state.eligible_listings_for_session(current_day)` and prepends converted player lots to `session_lots`. Two new callbacks on AuctionView: `on_player_lot_sold(listing, sale_price)` credits `player.credits += sale_price`, sets `auction_first_sale` flag on first sale, fires `auto_auction_first_sale` journal entry, increments stat counter via the model. `on_player_lot_withdrawn(listing)` returns the item to inventory (commodity → `ship.add_cargo`, part → `parts_inventory[id] += quantity`), sets `auction_first_listing_withdrawn` flag on first withdrawal, fires `auto_auction_first_listing_withdrawn`. News ticker emits a single anonymous headline for player sales >= 50,000 credits ("A consigned lot sells at Stellaris Auction House. Price undisclosed.").
- **Voice file extension** — 2 new top-level keys in `data/auctions/stellaris_voices.json`: `consigned_lot_lines` (4 Velo templates seller-anonymized + 1 SellLotView empty-inventory line) and `player_listing_post_session` (4 Sable post-session-read templates covering sold-above-reserve, sold-near-reserve, withdrawn-no-bids, withdrawn-bids-below-reserve). All in their respective voice registers. SA-B3's existing keys are NOT modified.
- **Polish fold-in #1 — FirstTimeTipOverlay on first SellLotView entry.** Flag `seen_first_listing_tip`. Copy: short, declarative, no flavor — "Listing fee is charged whether the lot sells or not. Set a reserve to refuse low bids." "Got it." dismiss button. Mirrors `seen_auction_first_session_tip`.
- **Polish fold-in #2 — 3 flag-gated journal entries.** `auto_auction_first_listing_created` (terse, in-fiction; player notes the fee is paid and the lot is on the floor); `auto_auction_first_sale` (records the hammer price concretely; no celebration); `auto_auction_first_listing_withdrawn` (records the reserve was not met and the item is back; the fee is gone). All voice-checked against the Writing Bible scanner AND `aurelia_voice_examples.md` 16-item diagnostic.
- **Polish fold-in #3 — Banter trigger flags + achievement stub.** 3 banter trigger flags (`auction_first_listing_created`, `auction_first_sale`, `auction_first_listing_withdrawn`) registered for SA-X6 consumption. Achievement stub `auction_seller` registered in `data/progression/achievements.json` with `stat_key="auction_listings_sold"`, `threshold=1`. SA-X7 owns final achievement metadata; SA-B5 owns the unlock condition (model counter increments on first player-seller-lot sold).
- **Tier-gated entry** — Stellaris Port standing tier `>= regular` (rep >= 0 per existing thresholds in `stellaris_tier_for_standing`) required to access the SellLotView. Sub-regular players see the "List a Lot" button rendered as locked with an inline tier-locked message. Listing creation also enforces the tier check at the model layer (`create_listing` returns `(False, "Listing requires Stellaris regular standing or above.")`).
- **Save/load coverage** — `AuctionState.to_dict` / `from_dict` extend with safe defaults for the 3 new fields and 3 new counters; `AuctionLot.to_dict` / `from_dict` round-trip the new optional `seller_id`; `_PlayerListing` carries its own `to_dict` / `from_dict`. Pre-SA-B5 saves load cleanly with empty listings + zero counters. Verified by round-trip test.
- **Tests** — 4 NEW test files (model, sell-lot-view, auction-view-player-listing addition, scenario, data-integrity-voice) covering ~25-35 new test functions across model methods, view lifecycle, scenario end-to-end, and voice-bible compliance.

**Acceptance criteria.**
1. `AuctionLot` gains optional `seller_id: Optional[str] = None` field. SA-B3 catalog (`stellaris_lots.json`) and SA-B4 catalog (`crimson_reach_lots.json`) load with `seller_id=None` for every lot. `to_dict` emits the field only when non-None — SA-B3/B4 lot dicts are unchanged on round-trip. Verified by `tests/test_models/test_bidding_player_listing.py::TestSellerIdField`.
2. `_PlayerListing` frozen dataclass round-trips through `to_dict`/`from_dict` cleanly. Old saves predating SA-B5 load with empty `active_listings` and `listing_history` and zero `auction_listings_sold` / `auction_listings_attempted` / `auction_listing_fees_paid` counters per §8.3 migration discipline. Verified by `TestAuctionStateMigration`.
3. `AuctionState.create_listing` validates: (a) item kind in {"commodity", "part"}; (b) item exists in player inventory at quantity >= requested; (c) declared_appraisal > 0; (d) reserve_pct in [0.50, 0.95]; (e) `len(active_listings) < MAX_ACTIVE_LISTINGS=3`; (f) player Stellaris tier >= "regular"; (g) player credits >= computed fee. Failure cases each return distinct `(False, str)` messages without mutating state. Success deducts fee from credits, deducts item from inventory, appends `_PlayerListing` to `active_listings`, increments `auction_listings_attempted`, increments `auction_listing_fees_paid`. Verified parametrically across all 7 failure paths and the success path.
4. Listing fee math: `fee = max(LISTING_FEE_FLOOR, int(declared_appraisal * LISTING_FEE_RATE))` = `max(100, int(declared * 0.05))`. Boundary-tested at appraisals 0 / 1 / 1999 / 2000 / 50000 / 1000000. Fee is paid in either sale outcome (sold or withdrawn); never refunded.
5. `cancel_listing(listing_id, player)` succeeds only when the listing is still `active` (not already pulled into a live session); returns the item to player inventory; does NOT refund the fee. Failure path (listing already in active session) returns `(False, "Listing is already on the auction floor; cannot cancel.")`. Verified by `TestCancelListing`.
6. `eligible_listings_for_session(current_day)` returns up to `MAX_ACTIVE_LISTINGS=3` listings whose `listed_on_day <= current_day`. Listings already converted to lots in a prior session (tracked by listing id presence in any active session lot) are excluded.
7. Player-seller lot resolution: when a session lot has `seller_id == "player"` and `_resolve_lot` fires, on `sold=True` the listing dict moves to `listing_history` with `outcome="sold"` + `sale_price` + `closed_on_day`; `auction_listings_sold` increments. On `sold=False` (reserve not met), the listing dict moves to `listing_history` with `outcome="withdrawn"`; `auction_listings_sold` does NOT increment. Verified by `TestResolvePlayerLot`.
8. `_prepare_stellaris_session` integrates eligible player listings: when called with the player having 1+ eligible `active_listings`, the prepared `session_lots` list begins with the converted player lots followed by the catalog lots, capped at the standard or headliner session size; persona attendance and speculator-category cycling are unaffected. When the player has zero eligible listings, behavior is byte-identical to SA-B3's pre-SA-B5 prepare flow. Verified by `tests/test_scenarios/test_scenario_player_listing.py::TestSessionPreparation`.
9. AuctionView PREVIEW: at `venue_id == "stellaris"` AND player Stellaris tier >= `regular`, the "List a Lot" button renders and routes to `GameState.SELL_LOT` on press. At tier < `regular`, the button renders disabled with a tier-locked label ("Stellaris regular standing required."). At `venue_id == "crimson_reach"`, the button does NOT render. The "Active Listings" subsection renders one row per listing in `auction_state.active_listings`. Verified by `tests/test_views/test_auction_view_player_listing.py::TestPreviewListingAffordances`.
10. AuctionView BID_WINDOW for player-seller lots: when the active lot has `seller_id == "player"`, raise/hold/fold buttons are NOT rendered (they are the only player-action surface, and the player is the seller — they cannot bid on their own lot); a "Your lot — watching" banner renders instead; AI bidders behave normally; the round timer + AI counter-bid logic are unchanged. Player-as-bidder lots (catalog lots) render the standard bid UI. Verified by `TestBidWindowPlayerSeller`.
11. AuctionView LOT_RESOLUTION for player-seller lots: `sold` outcome renders "Sold for {sale_price:,} credits."; `withdrawn` outcome renders "Reserve not met. The lot returns to your hold."; both messages voice-check clean. Verified by `TestLotResolutionPlayerSeller`.
12. AuctionView POST_SESSION: when at least one player lot resolved in the session AND Sable is on crew, a Sable line from `player_listing_post_session` renders (bucket selected by outcome — sold-above-reserve / sold-near-reserve / withdrawn-no-bids / withdrawn-bids-below-reserve); when Sable is not on crew, the line is omitted; when no player lot resolved this session, the line is omitted. Voice-check clean. Verified by `TestPostSessionPlayerListing`.
13. SellLotView lifecycle: `on_enter` calls `super().on_enter()` and creates UI elements; `on_exit` calls `super().on_exit()` and destroys all UI elements (no leaks). FirstTimeTipOverlay fires on first entry (flag `seen_first_listing_tip`); on second entry the overlay does NOT fire. Empty-state renders the `consigned_lot_lines.empty_inventory` voice line when player has zero eligible items. Tier-locked branch renders the inline lock message and disables Confirm when player tier < `regular`. Verified by `tests/test_views/test_sell_lot_view.py`.
14. SellLotView form behavior: declared-appraisal field rejects non-positive integers; reserve-pct slider clamps to [0.50, 0.95] with default 0.70; fee-preview updates live with declared-appraisal changes; Confirm button enabled only when all gates pass (tier >= regular, slot count < 3, sufficient credits, valid form). Confirm with valid form calls `auction_state.create_listing(...)`, sets `auction_first_listing_created` flag if first time, fires `auto_auction_first_listing_created` journal entry, returns to `GameState.AUCTION`. Confirm failure renders error-state UI from the returned `(False, msg)`.
15. Engine callbacks: on player-lot sale, `on_player_lot_sold(listing, sale_price)` credits `player.credits += sale_price`, sets `auction_first_sale` flag if first time, fires `auto_auction_first_sale` journal entry. On player-lot withdrawal, `on_player_lot_withdrawn(listing)` returns the item to inventory (commodity via `ship.add_cargo(item_id, quantity, price_per_unit=0)`; part via `parts_inventory[item_id] += quantity`), sets `auction_first_listing_withdrawn` flag if first time, fires `auto_auction_first_listing_withdrawn` journal entry. Verified end-to-end in the scenario test.
16. News ticker integration: player sales with hammer price >= 50,000 credits emit a single anonymous headline ("A consigned lot sells at Stellaris Auction House. Price undisclosed."); sales below the threshold emit no headline. Verified by parametric test.
17. Voice content for `consigned_lot_lines` (4 Velo templates + 1 empty-inventory) reads in Velo's ceremonial register (matches the cadence of `velo_lines` templates per a static keyword/sentence-length scan); seller-anonymized (no "{player_name}" substitutions). Voice content for `player_listing_post_session` (4 Sable templates) does not collapse into universal-wisdom register (sentence-length distribution + diagnostic-keyword scan from `aurelia_voice_examples.md`). 3 new journal entries pass the Writing Bible scanner AND the 16-item diagnostic. Verified by `tests/test_data_integrity/test_player_listing_voice.py`.
18. Achievement stub `auction_seller` registered in `data/progression/achievements.json` with `stat_key: "auction_listings_sold"`, `threshold: 1`, `category: "economy"`, `hidden: true`. The existing AchievementManager picks up the entry without code changes. Player property `auction_listings_sold` returns `auction_state.auction_listings_sold`. `_mark_auction_seller_if_first` is NOT needed — the model counter increment is the unlock signal. Verified by `TestAuctionSellerAchievement`.
19. Full scenario (`tests/test_scenarios/test_scenario_player_listing.py`): with locked seed and seeded player input, a regular-tier player at Stellaris → enters SellLotView → consigns 1 cargo commodity (declared appraisal 8,000, reserve 0.70) → fee 400 credits deducted → item removed → listing appended → next scheduled session → player lot is first lot in session → AI buyers (deterministic) bid → lot sells at hammer price >= reserve_price → player credited → first-sale journal + flag fires → counter increments. Second branch: regular-tier player consigns a second lot with reserve 0.95 → AI bids stop below reserve → withdrawn → item returned → fee NOT refunded → first-withdrawal journal + flag fires.
20. SA-B2 / SA-B3 / SA-B4 locked decisions are NOT re-litigated. SA-B5 only adds new player-seller-specific decisions and content; SA-B3's Stellaris artifacts (Velo dialogue tree, SA-B3 lot catalog) are extended additively (2 new voice keys); SA-B4's Reach artifacts are NOT modified. AI persona behavior is unchanged — `compute_effective_value` and `compute_ceiling` work bilaterally because they read `lot.category` + `lot.base_appraisal`, not seller identity.
21. Pre-phase test baseline preserved: pass count >= 9780; no new failures vs. baseline. New tests bring the count to roughly 9810-9825 passing. Touched-files-only `ruff format` + `ruff check` + `mypy` clean. Writing Bible scanner clean. Dialogue-integrity scanner clean. SI-3 flag scanner clean.

**Risks / open questions.**
- ~~What can the player list?~~ **LOCKED §B5.1**: Items in `player.ship.current_cargo` (any commodity) AND `player.parts_inventory` (any ship part). NOT listable: `unlocked_modules` (boss-drop legendary set per §11.10), `ground_equipment`, `salvage_hold_manager` contents (must transfer to cargo first), installed ship equipment. *Rationale*: keeps SA-B5 on a clean ship-side eligibility surface; preserves the boss-drop loop for legendary modules; aligns with player intuition that "items in my hold" is what gets consigned.
- ~~Which venue(s) accept player listings?~~ **LOCKED §B5.2**: Stellaris Auction House only. Crimson Reach Black Market does NOT accept player listings in SA-B5. *Rationale*: Stellaris's calendar-based session schedule maps cleanly to listing scheduling; Reach's demand-driven cadence makes "schedule a player lot" awkward; Reach's no-questions-asked culture is more naturally a buyer-side experience. SA-B6 polish may consider adding Reach player listings if playtest demands it.
- ~~How do player lots integrate with sessions?~~ **LOCKED §B5.3**: Player lots are prepended to the next scheduled Stellaris session's `session_lots` list. Up to 3 player lots per session (capped by `MAX_ACTIVE_LISTINGS`); session size is unchanged (catalog lots are dropped from the tail to make room if needed). AI buyer pool is the existing 3 named rivals + 2 Stellaris Speculators — bilaterally compatible because persona value functions read `lot.category` + `lot.base_appraisal`. *Rationale*: maximizes engine reuse (§11.11); player experiences a session that contains both their consignment and the AI catalog, reinforcing the "I'm participating in the economy" framing from `station_anchors.md:151`.
- ~~Listing fee structure.~~ **LOCKED §B5.4**: `fee = max(LISTING_FEE_FLOOR=100, int(declared_appraisal * LISTING_FEE_RATE=0.05))`. Fee is paid up front at listing creation; never refunded (sold OR withdrawn OR cancelled). *Rationale*: 5% rate is below typical e-commerce listing fees but above zero — a perceptible cost; floor of 100 prevents fee abuse on micro-listings; non-refundable behavior matches the design doc's "listing fee charged regardless of sale" deliverable. SA-B6 may tune.
- ~~Reserve price interaction.~~ **LOCKED §B5.5**: Player sets `reserve_pct` in [0.50, 0.95], default 0.70. Reserve price is hidden from AI buyers (mirroring §5.4). Below 0.50 not allowed (the "give it away" floor — Stellaris doesn't accept consignments where the reserve is half value or less; this is also a balance lever to prevent player-listing arbitrage). SA-B5 ships only non-contraband listings (`contraband=False` on the converted lot); contraband listings would carry legality-consequence math that has not been designed for the player-as-seller direction. *Rationale*: locks the reserve range tight so playtest can validate; defers contraband listings to SA-B6.
- ~~Listing slot limit.~~ **LOCKED §B5.6**: `MAX_ACTIVE_LISTINGS = 3`. Player can have at most 3 listings active simultaneously. Cancellation frees a slot (without refunding the fee); a sold or withdrawn listing also frees a slot at session close. *Rationale*: matches the design-doc deliverable text ("configurable, e.g., 3 active at a time"); 3 is enough to feel meaningful without becoming a market-manipulation surface for the player. SA-B6 may tune.
- ~~Where does the player initiate a listing?~~ **LOCKED §B5.7**: New `SellLotView` at `spacegame/views/sell_lot_view.py` accessed from the AuctionView's PREVIEW substate via a "List a Lot" button. New `GameState.SELL_LOT`. Routes back to `GameState.AUCTION` on confirm or back. NOT a modal inside AuctionView (the form is large enough — item-selection list, declared-appraisal input, reserve slider, fee preview — to justify its own view); NOT a separate hub-card location (avoids hub clutter and keeps the player's mental model "this is the auction house's other side"). *Rationale*: separates concerns cleanly; matches the BaseView lifecycle pattern per `views/CLAUDE.md`.
- ~~Velo's voice for player lots.~~ **LOCKED §B5.8**: Velo announces player-listed lots in his ceremonial register but seller-anonymized — no "{player_name}" substitution, no "consigned by Captain X" tag. The lot is identifiable only by category and headline. New `consigned_lot_lines` voice key in `stellaris_voices.json` carries 4 Velo templates (lot-open, "we are at X", lot-closed-sold, lot-closed-withdrawn) + 1 SellLotView empty-inventory line. *Rationale*: keeps the seller's identity ambiguous for narrative texture; mirrors real auction-house anonymity for consigned lots; avoids the awkward case where Velo announces the player's own name during the player's session.
- ~~CaptainMemory effects when an AI rival wins a player lot.~~ **LOCKED §B5.9**: NO `OUTCOME_OUTBID` or other CaptainMemory entry fires when an AI rival wins a player-listed lot. The player isn't *losing* — the rival is *paying the player*. New outcome constants are NOT introduced. *Rationale*: keeps Captain Memory focused on adversarial encounters; a rival buying from the player is a positive-sum interaction, not a rivalry tension; design doc §6.3 is intentionally narrow ("player loses to rival in same lot") and SA-B5 does not extend it.
- ~~Tier-gated entry.~~ **LOCKED §B5.10**: Stellaris Port standing tier `>= "regular"` (rep >= 0 per `stellaris_tier_for_standing`) required to access SellLotView and create listings. Apprentice players see the "List a Lot" button rendered as locked with a tier-locked message. Listing creation enforces the tier check at the model layer too (defence in depth). *Rationale*: institutional venues don't accept consignments from unproven sellers; mirrors real auction houses; gives the apprentice tier a concrete progression target ("regular tier unlocks consignment").
- ~~First-time tip overlay.~~ **LOCKED §B5.11**: New tip flag `seen_first_listing_tip()` per SI-3 cookbook. Copy: "Listing fee is charged whether the lot sells or not. Set a reserve to refuse low bids." Fires on first entry to SellLotView. *Rationale*: this is the kind of mechanic where blind-firsting is punishing (the player loses the fee on a withdrawn listing); a one-shot tip teaches the irreversibility of the fee and the role of the reserve, then never fires again. Onboarding §(a) overlay style.
- ~~Polish fold-in scope.~~ **LOCKED §B5.12**: 3 flag-gated journal entries + 3 banter trigger flags + 1 achievement stub (`auction_seller`) + 1 first-time tip overlay fold into SA-B5. Crew banter content (SA-X6), achievement metadata text (SA-X7), per-venue visual identity refinement (SA-X10), tutorial-pass refinement (SA-X3), cross-anchor narrative threading (SA-X1), reputation-balance pass (SA-X2), and Reach player-listing variant (SA-B6) all stay in their own sprints. *Rationale*: matches SA-B3 / SA-B4 polish discipline.
- ~~Test-file boundary.~~ **LOCKED §B5.13**: SA-B5 adds 5 new test files. Does NOT modify SA-B2 / SA-B3 / SA-B4 test classes; extends the data-loader test only if the loader needs new logic (it does not — the additional voice keys flow through unchanged). *Rationale*: keeps the engine-vs-content boundary clean; prior sprints' tests stay untouched.
- **OPEN — defer to implementation**: Whether the player-listing inserts into the *very next* Stellaris session deterministically, or has its own draw weight that competes with catalog lots for inclusion. SA-B5 implementer ships the deterministic-prepend behavior (locked §B5.3); if playtest reveals the player's lots dominate sessions and the AI catalog feels squeezed, SA-B6 may introduce a draw-weight mechanic. Default to deterministic prepend for SA-B5 — predictability is more important than balance at this stage.
- **OPEN — defer to implementation**: Whether listings can be *cancelled* after the session preview opens but before the lot is called. **Decisions locked in this planning phase.**

1. **Listable items**: ship cargo (`current_cargo`) AND parts inventory (`parts_inventory`). NOT listable: `unlocked_modules` (boss-drop set per §11.10), `ground_equipment`, `salvage_hold_manager` contents, installed equipment.
2. **Listing venue**: Stellaris Auction House only. Crimson Reach player listings deferred to SA-B6.
3. **Session integration**: Player lots prepended to the next scheduled Stellaris session's `session_lots`; up to 3 per session per `MAX_ACTIVE_LISTINGS`; AI buyer pool unchanged.
4. **Listing fee structure**: `fee = max(LISTING_FEE_FLOOR=100, int(declared_appraisal * LISTING_FEE_RATE=0.05))`; non-refundable in any outcome.
5. **Reserve range**: `reserve_pct` in [0.50, 0.95], default 0.70. Hidden from AI buyers (mirrors §5.4). Contraband listings out of scope for SA-B5.
6. **Listing slot limit**: `MAX_ACTIVE_LISTINGS = 3`. Cancellation frees a slot but does not refund the fee.
7. **Listing UI surface**: NEW `SellLotView` + `GameState.SELL_LOT`; accessed from AuctionView PREVIEW substate; routes back on confirm or back. NOT a modal; NOT a separate hub-card location.
8. **Velo's voice for player lots**: ceremonial register, seller-anonymized. New `consigned_lot_lines` voice key with 4 Velo templates + 1 SellLotView empty-inventory line.
9. **CaptainMemory effects**: NONE. AI rivals winning a player lot is positive-sum and does not record an outcome. Design doc §6.3 stays narrowly about adversarial encounters.
10. **Tier-gated entry**: Stellaris Port standing tier `>= "regular"` (rep >= 0). Sub-regular sees a tier-locked lock message; model-layer check too (defence in depth).
11. **First-time tip overlay**: NEW flag `seen_first_listing_tip`. Copy: "Listing fee is charged whether the lot sells or not. Set a reserve to refuse low bids."
12. **Polish fold-in scope**: 3 flag-gated journal entries + 3 banter trigger flags + 1 achievement stub (`auction_seller`) + 1 first-time tip overlay fold into SA-B5. Crew banter content (SA-X6), achievement metadata (SA-X7), per-venue visual identity (SA-X10), tutorial-pass refinement (SA-X3), cross-anchor narrative (SA-X1), reputation-balance (SA-X2), Reach player-listing variant (SA-B6) all stay in their own sprints.
13. **Test-file boundary**: SA-B5 adds 5 NEW test files. Does NOT modify SA-B2/B3/B4 test classes. Voice file is extended additively — SA-B3's existing keys untouched.

**Deliverables.**

- **Bidding tuning notes** — `requirements/sa_bidding_tuning_notes.md` authored fresh. Sections: (1) methodology — how the implementer collected playtest signal (manual scenario walkthrough using the existing scenario tests as drivers, plus deterministic ceiling/aggression sweeps); (2) observed signal — concrete observations from running synthetic sessions across the 5 personas at 2 rep tiers and 2 venues, noting which lots feel under- or over-priced and which personas dominate or sit out; (3) recommended adjustments per category (persona ceiling_ratio, persona aggression, listing fee rate, Reach demand probability, min increment scale) — each recommendation paired with a one-line "applied" or "deferred to future sprint" decision; (4) applied changes — the actual constants edited, with before/after values; (5) skip list — categories examined and intentionally NOT adjusted, with the reason. The doc is the audit trail; the sprint's actual constant changes are the smaller, targeted edits in code.

- **Post-session line rotation (SA-B3 review's single tighten).** `auction_view._post_session_lines()` (lines 1101-1171) currently selects `options[0]` from each rival's bucket array. SA-B6 changes the selection to `options[_seed_index(session_id, rival_id, bucket) % len(options)]` where `_seed_index` is a module-local helper that hashes the three-tuple deterministically. Result: across sessions, each authored 3-option array surfaces all three lines over time; within a single session the rotation is deterministic so save/load reproduces the same line. Stellaris benefits immediately (its post-session buckets ship 3 options each); Reach benefits once deliverable below extends its buckets to 2-3 each.

- **Reach Salko post-session bucket expansion.** Each of the four Salko buckets in `crimson_reach_voices.json` (`rival_won`, `player_won`, `no_overlap`, `absent_retired`) currently ships 1 line. SA-B6 extends each to 2-3 lines so the rotation has material to draw from at Reach. The new lines are voice-checked against Salko's voice sheet (cold-grudge register, present-tense, brief, honorifics absent, theatrical reaction absent); against the 16-item diagnostic; and against the existing Reach voice file's tone (the buckets coexist with Vex Tarn's terse declarative auctioneer lines). Existing first-line content in each bucket is preserved as the `[0]` entry to keep deterministic prior behavior under any test that locked an exact line.

- **Dead-code removal (SA-B2 review's single tighten).** `auction_view.update()` contains an `on_session_complete` delta-detection block at roughly line 335 that fires when `len(st.session_history) > prior_history_count`. The SA-B2 review noted this branch is unreachable because `session_history` increments inside `handle_event` (via `_handle_button` → `advance_after_resolution`) before `update()` runs the next frame; the live `on_session_complete` callback is now driven from `_handle_button`'s `_maybe_fire_session_complete()`. SA-B6 removes the dead branch and its prior_history_count tracking, runs the existing tests to confirm the callback still fires from the active path, and adds an explicit test that asserts the callback is invoked from button handling, not from `update()`.

- **`OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED` constant + symmetric rivalry resolution.** Per design-doc §10.5, SA-B6 introduces `OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED = "outcompeted"` in `spacegame/models/captain_memory.py` next to `OUTCOME_OUTBID`. Behavior is identical to `OUTCOME_OUTBID` from the `record_encounter` perspective (increments `encounter_count`, updates `last_seen_day`, sets `last_outcome`, no immediate status transition; auto-retires to `STATUS_WANDERER` after `RESOLUTION_THRESHOLD = 3` accumulated entries). In `bidding.py::_record_rival_outcomes`, when the resolved lot's winner is the player AND a named rival was a recorded bidder on that lot, record `OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED` against that rival. Symmetric to the existing `OUTCOME_OUTBID` path; both share `RESOLUTION_THRESHOLD`. Player abstention (Hold/Fold) suppresses the entry on both sides.

- **Accessibility audit.** A targeted pass over `auction_view.py` and `sell_lot_view.py` against `ui_design_standards.md`'s compliance checklist plus a small additional gate-list: (a) keyboard navigation through the bid panel (Raise / Hold / Fold and the Speed selector are reachable via Tab order); (b) no critical information conveyed by color alone (the BID_WINDOW high-bid display reads the value as text; the speed selector reads the active speed via label, not just a highlight color); (c) the FirstTimeTipOverlay's body text is left-aligned within the panel and does not overflow at 1280×720 minimum resolution; (d) the speed selector's "slow" mode (45 s rounds, 5 s snipe) is concretely usable for slow-input players (verified by walking the existing scenario test at slow speed). Any concrete fixes that surface during the audit are folded into the auction_view / sell_lot_view edits; if no fixes surface, the audit's pass result is recorded in the tuning notes. Lock: SA-B6 does NOT add a "pause" or "auto-bid" affordance — those are scope creep beyond a tuning sprint.

- **Closed-out decision documentation.** Four open SA-B2/B5 questions are LOCKED in this planning phase as design decisions (NOT executed): (1) Reach player-listing variant — permanently deferred, not in scope; (2) listing draw-weight vs. deterministic prepend — deterministic prepend stays; (3) listing cancellation window — pre-session-only, the SA-B5 review's floor guard is the final state; (4) `velo_lines` → `auctioneer_lines` rename — alias is permanent infrastructure, not transitional. Each is recorded under the sprint's locked decisions section with a one-line rationale.

- **Tests** — 1 new test class in `test_bidding_captain_memory.py` (4-6 tests for OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED accumulation + auto-retire), 1 new test class in `test_auction_view.py` (3-4 tests for post-session rotation determinism + dead-code path removal), extension to `test_auction_view_reach.py` (1-2 tests for expanded Salko buckets), extension to `test_bidding_state.py` (1-2 tests for player-win-streak rivalry resolution), extension to `test_reach_voice_compliance.py` (1 test for bucket-shape >= 2 options). Approximate count: 10-15 new tests.

**Acceptance criteria.**
1. `requirements/sa_bidding_tuning_notes.md` exists with the 5 sections specified (methodology / observed signal / recommended adjustments / applied changes / skip list). The applied-changes table lists each constant changed with before/after values; the skip-list table lists each category examined and explicitly not adjusted, with one-line rationale per row. Voice-checked against Writing Bible scanner over any player-facing copy stubs (the doc itself is internal and does not need scanner coverage, but any copy stubs it cites do).
2. `OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED = "outcompeted"` constant is defined in `spacegame/models/captain_memory.py` adjacent to the existing `OUTCOME_OUTBID` constant. Constant value is the lowercase string `"outcompeted"` to match the existing convention. The existing valid-outcomes set (or any module-level allowlist) includes the new constant if such a set exists; otherwise the constant participates implicitly through `record_encounter`'s string-tolerant behavior.
3. Symmetric rivalry resolution: when `_record_rival_outcomes` fires on a `LOT_RESOLUTION` and `record.winner_id == "player"` AND a named rival placed at least one bid on that lot, exactly one `OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED` entry fires against that rival. Three accumulated `OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED` entries against the same rival auto-retire that captain to `STATUS_WANDERER` via the existing `record_encounter` threshold path. Player abstention (Hold or Fold) suppresses the entry. Mixed `OUTCOME_OUTBID` + `OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED` entries against the same rival both count toward the same `RESOLUTION_THRESHOLD = 3`. Verified by `tests/test_models/test_bidding_captain_memory.py::TestOutcomeOutcompeted` (single record, 3-record auto-retire, abstention suppression, mixed-outcome aggregation).
4. Post-session line rotation: `_post_session_lines()` selects from each rival's bucket array using a deterministic seed derived from `(session_id, rival_id, bucket_name)`. Across three distinct session ids against a fixture rival bucket containing 3 authored options, each authored option is selected at least once. Within a single session id, the rotation is stable: calling `_post_session_lines()` twice with the same session id returns the same selection. Verified by `tests/test_views/test_auction_view.py::TestPostSessionRotation`.
5. Reach Salko bucket expansion: each of the four `post_session.fenn_salko.{rival_won, player_won, no_overlap, absent_retired}` arrays in `crimson_reach_voices.json` has at least 2 entries (target 2-3 each). The first entry in each bucket matches the SA-B4 line byte-for-byte to preserve deterministic prior behavior in any test that captured an exact line. New lines pass the Writing Bible scanner and the 16-item diagnostic; sentence length stays consistent with Salko's voice sheet (no theatrical reaction, no honorifics, present tense, terse). Verified by `tests/test_data_integrity/test_reach_voice_compliance.py::test_salko_buckets_offer_variety` and the existing voice-bible scan.
6. Dead-code removal: the `on_session_complete` delta-detection block in `auction_view.update()` (around line 335 where `len(st.session_history) > prior_history_count` is checked) is removed along with its `prior_history_count` tracking. The `on_session_complete` callback continues to fire correctly via `_handle_button`'s `_maybe_fire_session_complete()`. A test asserts that draining a multi-lot session through `_handle_button` triggers the callback exactly once, while a parallel call into `update()` (no button event) does NOT trigger it.
7. Tuning adjustments are applied OR explicitly skipped. For each of the five categories (persona ceiling_ratio, persona aggression, listing fee rate, Reach demand probability, min increment scale), the tuning notes document either an applied change (constant edit + before/after value) or an explicit skip (with one-line rationale). At least one category is examined in detail in the methodology section, even if the conclusion is "no change". Existing scenario tests stay green under any applied changes.
8. Accessibility audit pass: the audit results are documented in the tuning notes' "applied changes" section under an "Accessibility" subsection. Concrete fixes (if any) are committed; if no fixes surface, the audit's pass-state is recorded explicitly. The audit checks: (a) Tab order through bid-panel buttons is sequential; (b) no critical info is color-only; (c) FirstTimeTipOverlay text fits within the panel at 1280×720; (d) "slow" speed setting completes a full scenario walkthrough deterministically. No new UI affordances are added; the audit is verification + small fixes only.
9. SA-B5 review's floor guard remains in place: `cancel_listing` still rejects cancellation once a listing is on the active session floor. SA-B6 explicitly does NOT extend the cancellation window (locked decision §B6.3); the existing `TestCancelListing::test_cancel_blocked_when_lot_on_active_floor` stays green.
10. All existing acceptance criteria from SA-B2 / SA-B3 / SA-B4 / SA-B5 stay satisfied. SA-B6 does NOT regress: bidding lifecycle, lot pool generation, persona value functions, save/load round-trip, journal/news/achievement firings, voice-bible compliance, dialogue-integrity scanner, SI-3 flag scanner all remain clean.
11. Pre-phase test baseline preserved: pass count >= 9881; skip count == 98; no new failures vs. baseline. New tests bring the count to roughly 9890-9900 passing. Touched-files-only `ruff format` + `ruff check` + `mypy` clean. Writing Bible scanner clean. Dialogue-integrity scanner clean. SI-3 flag scanner clean.
12. UI compliance against `ui_design_standards.md`: the auction-view + sell-lot-view audit's pass result is recorded; any `requirements/ui_design_standards.md` core-principle violations found during the audit are either fixed inline or filed as a follow-up item in the tuning notes (not as a new sprint, unless the violation is large enough to warrant one — in which case escalate via PHASE_BLOCKED).

10. **Status flip to `review` + phase report + commit (~15 min).** Move `Status` to `review`. Append `**Last phase report.**` block (overwriting any prior phase report block in this section). Commit with `SA-B6: ...` prefix. Do NOT push. Touches: `requirements/roadmap/ROADMAP.md`.

**Decisions locked in this planning phase.**

1. **§B6.1 Tuning sprint scope.** SA-B6 is restricted to (a) constant adjustments documented in the tuning notes; (b) authored-content additions to existing voice files; (c) the polish items called out in SA-B2/B3/B4/B5 review reports; (d) `OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED` for symmetric rivalry resolution; (e) the accessibility audit. SA-B6 does NOT add new lots, new personas, new venues, new view substates, new constants, or new persona archetypes. *Rationale*: keeps the M-sized boundary credible; the design-doc §10 deferred items list calls SA-B6 a "tuning + balance" sprint and SA-B3/B4/B5 already handled the heavyweight content/integration work.

2. **§B6.2 Reach player-listing variant — permanently deferred.** The SA-B5 §B5.2 deferral note flagged Reach player listings for "SA-B6 polish may consider adding... if playtest demands it." Locked: Reach player listings are NOT added in SA-B6 and are NOT proposed as a follow-up sprint. *Rationale*: the SA-B5 §B5.2 rationale ("Stellaris's calendar-based session schedule maps cleanly to listing scheduling; Reach's demand-driven cadence makes 'schedule a player lot' awkward; Reach's no-questions-asked culture is more naturally a buyer-side experience") survives playtest review — Reach as a buyer-side experience is the design intent, not a workaround. Forcing a consignment-side surface at Reach would require a Floor Manager voice for player-anonymous lots that does not exist and would dilute the Floor Manager's terse declarative register. Closed.

3. **§B6.3 Listing cancellation window — pre-session-only, no extension.** The SA-B5 OPEN-defer note flagged whether listings could be cancelled after preview opens but before the lot is called. The SA-B5 review's floor-guard fix (`cancel_listing` rejects cancellation once a listing is on the active floor) is the final cancellation contract. SA-B6 does NOT extend this window. *Rationale*: extending the window adds user-visible state to the AuctionView (a "Cancel listing" button mid-session) and complicates the pre-session-vs-active-session split; the listing fee is non-refundable in any outcome, so the window extension provides little player benefit. Pre-session cancellation is sufficient.

4. **§B6.4 Listing draw-weight — deterministic prepend stays.** The SA-B5 OPEN-defer note flagged whether player listings should compete with catalog lots for inclusion via a draw weight. Locked: deterministic prepend stays (the SA-B5 default). *Rationale*: predictability is more valuable than balance for the player-as-seller experience — a player who consigns a lot expecting it to appear in the next session should see it appear in the next session, not a session two cycles later because the draw weight rolled poorly. The 3-listing cap (`MAX_ACTIVE_LISTINGS = 3`) plus the existing session-size cap already prevents the player from dominating the session catalog.

5. **§B6.5 `OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED` — implemented for symmetric rivalry resolution.** Per design-doc §10.5, SA-B6 introduces the constant and wires the symmetric path: a player who beats a named rival three sessions in a row auto-retires that rival to `STATUS_WANDERER`, mirroring the existing `OUTCOME_OUTBID` accumulation against player losses. *Rationale*: without this, the auto-retire path is one-directional — losing 3 times to a rival retires them, but winning 3 times against them leaves the rival in `STATUS_ACTIVE` indefinitely. Asymmetric rivalry resolution feels punitive to skilled players; symmetric is the right fairness contract. The `record_encounter` threshold fall-through already covers the auto-retire transition without code changes — the new constant is purely additive. Mixed `OUTCOME_OUTBID` + `OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED` aggregate against the same `RESOLUTION_THRESHOLD = 3` so a rivalry that toggles between wins and losses still resolves at the natural threshold.

6. **§B6.6 Voice-key alias rename — alias is permanent infrastructure.** The SA-B4 §B4.6 lock flagged a possible rename of `velo_lines` → `auctioneer_lines` in `stellaris_voices.json` for cross-venue consistency. Locked: NOT executed. *Rationale*: the rename adds zero behavior change, breaks deterministic round-trip on existing test fixtures and saves, and the `auction_view._velo_running_commentary` alias fallback (`auctioneer_lines` first, `velo_lines` second) is small, well-contained, and durable. Future venues authored in the SA-B4 pattern use `auctioneer_lines` natively; SA-B3's Stellaris file keeps `velo_lines` as a stable read-only artifact.

7. **§B6.7 Reach demand cadence — tunable, not redesigned.** The SA-B4 locked decision §B4.4 set `REACH_DEMAND_PROBABILITY = 0.35` and `REACH_DEMAND_MAX_GAP_DAYS = 8`. SA-B6 may tune these constants per the tuning notes, but does NOT redesign the demand mechanic (e.g., does not introduce a deterministic schedule or a player-controllable cadence). *Rationale*: the irregular feel is a Reach culture commitment; redesigning it would re-litigate SA-B4's locked design.

8. **§B6.8 Reach season tags — not added.** The SA-B4 locked decision §B4.11 flagged that "SA-B6 may add Reach-specific demand-tied seasons after playtest." Locked: NOT added. *Rationale*: the Reach culture's irregularity is precisely the contrast with Stellaris's calendar-driven seasons; adding seasons at Reach erodes the venue contrast. If the tuning notes' analysis surfaces a need, the implementer can flag it as a follow-up; SA-B6 does not implement it speculatively.

9. **§B6.9 Single-tighten polish items.** Three review-flagged single-tightens are explicitly in scope: post-session line rotation (SA-B3 review), dead `on_session_complete` block in `auction_view.update()` (SA-B2 review), and Reach Salko bucket expansion (SA-B4 review). *Rationale*: these are concrete reviewer-flagged debt items already documented in the SA-B2/B3/B4 review reports; closing them is part of the polish-pass commitment.

10. **§B6.10 No new sprints proposed.** SA-B6 closes out the SA-B2-B5 chain. No follow-up sprint is created for any deferred SA-B item. The blocks list (SA-X1/X2/X4/X5/X6/X7/X8/X9) covers downstream Phase VI work that uses Bidding artefacts. *Rationale*: a tuning sprint that proposes new sprints undermines its own role as the close-out; the right time to propose a Phase VII follow-up (if ever) is when Phase VI has shipped and surfaced a need.

11. **§B6.11 Test-file discipline.** SA-B6 extends existing test files (`test_bidding_captain_memory.py`, `test_auction_view.py`, `test_auction_view_reach.py`, `test_bidding_state.py`, `test_reach_voice_compliance.py`) and does NOT modify SA-B2/B3/B4/B5 test classes — additive only. *Rationale*: matches the test-file discipline locked in SA-B3 §B3.10, SA-B4 §B4.13, and SA-B5 §B5.13.

12. **§B6.12 Tuning-notes voice register.** The tuning notes doc is internal — engineering audit trail, not player-facing — so it does NOT require Writing Bible scanner coverage on its own prose. Any player-facing copy stubs the doc cites (e.g., journal entry templates that the implementer adjusts) DO require scanner coverage. *Rationale*: the scanner is for player-visible prose; reviewer-scoped engineering docs are exempt.

**Risks / open questions.**

- **Tuning subjectivity**: tuning is a judgment call, and the synthetic scenario tests are a proxy for playtest, not a substitute. The mitigation is the "applied vs. skipped" discipline in the tuning notes — every category gets a recorded decision with rationale, and "Skipped — within target range" is an accepted outcome. If the implementer cannot reach a confident decision on a category after one walkthrough, the right call is to skip and document, not to over-tune.
- **OUTCOME_OUTCOMPETED test surface**: the path through `record_encounter` is shared with `OUTCOME_OUTBID`, so the threshold-based auto-retire is exercised by existing tests. SA-B6 just adds the symmetric direction. The risk is a tests-have-locked-the-asymmetry gap — search for any test that asserts only OUTBID can drive the auto-retire and update if needed.
- **Post-session rotation deterministic test stability**: the seed must produce different selections across distinct session ids without producing collisions in unit tests. Use a hashing scheme that produces ints with sufficient spread (sha1 hex truncation works; modulo by `len(options)` distributes across the bucket).
- **Reach Salko bucket voice drift**: extending each bucket from 1 line to 2-3 lines doubles the surface area for voice-bible drift. The mitigation is tight: each new line must match Salko's `character_voices.md` voice sheet (cold-grudge, terse, no honorifics, present-tense, "states a number") and must pass the voice-distinct test that asserts the Floor Manager and Salko sets do not collapse into each other.
- **Accessibility-audit scope creep**: an audit can balloon into "redesign the bid panel" scope. The mitigation is the locked decision §B6.1 (no new affordances) and the audit's pre-defined checklist. If a violation is large enough to warrant a redesign, escalate via PHASE_BLOCKED.
- **Constant tuning regression risk**: a persona ceiling_ratio nudge can cascade into the deterministic scenario tests' expected sale prices. The mitigation is to run the full suite after each constant edit; if a test fails because the expected sale price changed, decide whether to update the test's expectation (legitimate tuning effect) or revert the constant change (test was capturing the prior balanced state).

### Phase IV — Research Patronage

#### SA-R1 — Okafor Institute (Research Patronage)

**Status**: done
**Phase**: Phase IV | **Size**: L | **Effort**: 2-3 weeks

**Goal.** Convert the Okafor Institute Medical Wing `unique` location at Axiom Labs into a working Research Patronage venue. Dr. Nadia Kweon (the Institute's current director, voice sheet authored in SA-PREP-1 at `character_voices.md` lines 659-708) presents 10 funded-research project templates rotating on a window. The player commits credits, optionally adds collaborator researchers (team-fund) at higher cost / shorter duration, then game-day ticks advance the active project to a deterministic outcome — success unlocks a payout plus a Patent/IP holding the player can license (passive royalties) or sell (lump-sum); failure forfeits part of the capital. Industry skill `research_yield` and Leadership skill `research_oversight` (both shipped in SA-C2) stack with Nuri Solberg's crew bonuses through the standard `crew_roster.get_bonus(...) + progression.get_bonus(...)` pattern.

**Deliverables.**
- New view (`OkaforView`) with a Kweon dock on the left, project-board panel listing 5-7 visible offers per visit (rolled deterministically from a 10-template pool against a 30-game-day window), and a separate "Active projects" panel listing the player's currently-funded projects with progress bars and an "Holdings" panel for completed Patents/IP.
- 10 research project templates spanning 3 risk tiers: 4× low-risk (5-10 day, 8-15k credits, modest payout, low failure odds), 4× mid-risk (10-20 day, 20-50k credits, larger payout, medium failure odds, some unlock module data), 2× high-risk (20-30 day, 50-150k credits, major payout, high failure odds, capstone unlocks). Each template names its consuming faction-flavor (Science Collective core; one Frontier Alliance medical-aid project; one Miners' Union industrial-medicine project) so faction-rep deltas on completion are non-uniform.
- Project-funding mechanic: solo-fund is the default; team-fund is an optional toggle that adds 0-2 collaborator slots from the team-fund roster (3 Institute researchers + Nuri Solberg crew if hired). Team-fund modifies the active project: cost ×1.5 per collaborator (capped at 2x with both), duration ×0.7 per collaborator (capped at 0.5 with both), success-payout split share routed to the Institute's relationship arc as +1 dialogue-flag tick per collaborator (`okafor_collaborator_share_<researcher_id>`). The math is documented inline in the model and the team-fund modal explains the trade-off in declarative copy.
- Risk dimension: each project carries a `base_failure_odds` (low: 0.05; mid: 0.18; high: 0.35). At resolution time, the failure check is deterministic: `rng = random.Random(f"{project_id}_{accept_game_day}_{player_seed}")` produces a single uniform value compared against `(base_failure_odds - research_risk_reduction_total)`. Save-scumming does not change the outcome (CLAUDE.md "Deterministic outcomes"). Failure refunds 30% of capital and emits a Kweon-voiced debrief; success pays the full success payout (modulated by `1.0 + research_yield_bonus_total`).
- Patent/IP dimension: every successful project produces a `PatentHolding` with three player-controllable states — `held` (default; no income; preserves the option), `licensed` (royalty: 5% of `success_payout` paid every 10 game-days while licensed; ends if licensed by another captain in a future expansion), `sold` (one-time lump-sum at 60% of `success_payout`; removes the holding). State transitions happen through Kweon's IP-disposition dialogue branch.

2. First entry to `OkaforView` fires the `FirstTimeTipOverlay` exactly once per save (gated on `seen_okafor_tip`). First conversation with Kweon sets `met_npc("kweon_director")` if not already set.
3. Project board renders 5-7 deterministic offers per visit. Re-entering on the same 30-day window produces the same offer set (deterministic seed `f"{game_day // 30}_{player_seed}_okafor"`); crossing the 30-day boundary forces a fresh roll. Already-funded projects are tracked separately in the "Active projects" panel and are NOT re-rolled.
4. Funding a project deducts credits, sets `OkaforResearchState.active_projects[project_id] = ActiveProject(accept_day, ...)` and decrements the available offer count for the current window so the same template cannot be funded twice in one window.
5. Game-day advance hook in `engine/game.py` (called wherever `Player.game_day` increments — see `Player.travel_to_system` line 478 and `Player.rest_at_station` line 501) ticks each active project; on `accept_day + duration_days`, the project resolves deterministically: failure check uses the seeded RNG against `(base_failure_odds - clamp(0, research_risk_reduction_total, base_failure_odds))`, success payout uses `success_payout * (1.0 + research_yield_bonus_total)`. Two saves of the same scenario produce identical outcomes.
6. Solo vs. team-fund are mechanically distinct and verified by parametric test: solo-fund of a 50k mid-tier project for 15 days yields baseline; team-fund with one collaborator yields cost 75k / duration 11 days; team-fund with two collaborators yields cost 100k / duration 8 days. Each collaborator slot sets `okafor_collaborator_share_<researcher_id>` on the project.
7. Skill stacking: `research_yield_bonus_total = crew_roster.get_bonus("research_yield_bonus") + progression.get_bonus("research_yield_bonus")` and `research_risk_reduction_total = crew_roster.get_bonus("research_risk_reduction") + progression.get_bonus("research_risk_reduction")`. With Nuri Solberg in the crew (+0.10 each) AND `research_yield` skill at level 2 AND `research_oversight` skill at level 2, total yield bonus is +0.20 and total risk reduction is +0.20. Verified by direct test against the integration in the view's resolution path.
8. Patent state machine: a successfully completed project produces a `PatentHolding` in `held` state. Player can transition to `licensed` (begins emitting `royalty_amount` credits every 10 game-days; verified by test that ticks 30 days and checks 3 royalty payouts) or `sold` (one-time payout at 60% of success payout, holding removed). Transitions go through Kweon's IP-disposition branch. `held` patents persist across saves; royalty schedule (next-payout-day) persists across saves.
9. Failure path: a project that resolves to failure refunds 30% of the original capital, sets the failure flag on the holdings list (no patent emitted), and triggers Kweon's failure-debrief dialogue exactly once for the FIRST failure (gated on `okafor_first_failure_seen`). Subsequent failures do not re-trigger the first-failure debrief but still emit the journal entry only on the first failure (entry deduped by trigger_flag).
10. Save/load: a save written with two active projects (one mid-risk, one high-risk), one held patent, one licensed patent (mid-cycle royalty schedule), and `kweon_relationship_value = 3` round-trips byte-clean for the SA-R1 fields. A legacy save with no `okafor_research_state` key loads as `state = None` (no errors).
11. Three new researcher NPC voice sheets are authored at the cast-variety standard (matching the Paz / Daro / Ife pattern from SA-1's R1 rework: Core voice, Verbal habits, Sample lines, distinct register). Names use no entries from the banned NPC list. Each researcher has a 3-node dialogue tree (greeting → project-context observation → sign-off) authored in `data/dialogue/dialogues.json`.

Kweon's institutional-fatigue register is held distinct from Nuri's methodology-rigor register and from the 3 researcher registers.

- ~~View / model file naming.~~ **LOCKED**: view is `spacegame/views/okafor_view.py`; model is `spacegame/models/okafor_research.py`; tests follow the same naming. *Rationale*: the SA-C2 design (`requirements/sa_skill_design.md` sections 1.6-1.7 and the bonus-naming table at 142-143) and the existing skill-wiring integration test (`tests/test_models/test_skill_wiring_integration.py:661-662`) both assert that `research_yield_bonus` and `research_risk_reduction` are consumed by `spacegame/views/okafor_view.py`. Venue-named files mirror SA-1 (`wreckers_guild_view.py`) and SA-2 (`deep_shafts_view.py`).
- ~~`GameState` enum value.~~ **LOCKED**: `GameState.OKAFOR = "okafor"`. *Rationale*: mirrors `WRECKERS_GUILD = "wreckers_guild"` and `DEEP_SHAFTS = "deep_shafts"`. The current draft used `GameState.RESEARCH`, which is system-named rather than venue-named; SA-R1 is a venue and the established pattern is venue-named.
- ~~Sub-reputation organization for the Institute.~~ **LOCKED**: NO sub-reputation org for Okafor. The vision text at `station_anchors.md:165` and Kweon's voice sheet describe a relationship arc (Kweon's trust accumulates with funded projects), not a membership/tier system. *Rationale*: tier-based sub-rep belongs to organizations that gate access by member rank (Wreckers' Guild's apprentice/journeyman/master). The Institute admits any captain who funds; the relationship is a dialogue-and-flag arc, not a numbered tier. Use `kweon_relationship_value: int` on `OkaforResearchState` (incremented on success, decremented on failure-debrief, range 0-10 clamp) so dialogue gates can read it without a full sub-rep config.
- ~~3 Institute researcher voice sheets — SA-PREP-1 coverage gap.~~ **LOCKED**: SA-R1 authors the 3 researcher voice sheets and appends them to `requirements/character_voices.md`'s SA Arc section as part of this sprint. *Rationale*: SA-PREP-1's NPC inventory (lines 585-616) catalogued only Kweon and Nuri Solberg for SA-R1; the "3-5 researcher NPCs" line in `station_anchors.md:165` was not folded into SA-PREP-1's table. Two paths existed: (a) block SA-R1 with PHASE_BLOCKED for an SA-PREP-1 follow-up, (b) fold the authoring into SA-R1 with a touch-zone extension. (b) is selected because the missing characters are tightly scoped to this venue, the cohesion-cost of blocking would be high, and authoring 3 lighter sheets (4 sections each — Core voice, Verbal habits, Sample lines, Bonus context — matching the SA-1 secondary-contact pattern) is a 2-3 hour task that fits inside the sprint's L sizing. The researchers' speaker_ids and dialogue trees are net-new in SA-R1's scope already, so the voice work goes alongside.
- ~~Project pool size.~~ **LOCKED**: 10 templates (mid-point of the 8-12 vision range). *Rationale*: 10 is enough to keep the 30-day window's 5-7-card roll feeling fresh across multiple visits at any tier; 12 was tempting but extends authoring + voice-check time without proportional player benefit.
- ~~Risk resolution determinism.~~ **LOCKED**: deterministic seed `random.Random(f"{project_id}_{accept_game_day}_{player_seed}")` evaluated at completion-tick time. *Rationale*: CLAUDE.md "Gameplay Philosophy" — "Deterministic outcomes: ... NOT random rolls. No save scumming." The risk profile is the visible probability the player commits against; the actual outcome is determined the moment the player funds, but only revealed at completion. Save-and-reload before completion does not change the result. This matches Aurelia's existing market-price determinism convention.
- ~~Solo vs. team-fund cost / duration math.~~ **LOCKED**: per collaborator: cost ×1.5, duration ×0.7, capped at 2 collaborators (final caps: cost 2.0×, duration 0.5×). Each collaborator slot sets a per-researcher dialogue flag. *Rationale*: makes the trade-off legible (more collaborators = more capital up-front, faster turnaround) without producing a degenerate "always team-fund" outcome at every point in the credit curve. The per-researcher flag plumbs into SA-R2's narrative arc, where Kweon's dialogue can reference which Institute staff the player has worked with.
- ~~Outcome unlocks scope.~~ **LOCKED**: outcomes consume existing entries in `data/ships/modules.json`, `data/ships/upgrades.json`, and `data/economy/commodities.json` market-availability flags. SA-R1 does NOT author new modules / upgrades / commodities. *Rationale*: the vision line "Outcomes unlock unique modules" is best served by elevating existing under-used items (a long-tail of modules / upgrades exist with limited vendor exposure) into research-gated unlocks. New module authoring is its own design surface; hiding it inside SA-R1 would expand scope past L. If the implementer finds outcomes unavoidable that would require new entries, log `SA-R1-FOLLOW-1` and ship a placeholder unlock pointing at the closest existing entry.
- ~~Polish fold-in scope.~~ **LOCKED**: tutorial first-time tip overlay AND four flag-gated journal entries AND save/load round-trip fold into SA-R1. - ~~Existing `axiom_labs_investment` basic-investment card.~~ **LOCKED**: PRESERVE. SA-R1 does not modify the existing investment card or its config (if it has one in `data/economy/investment_configs.json`). *Rationale*: per `requirements/investment_rewards_design.md` line 40, basic-investment-card returns at 10 systems remain in scope for future iteration. SA-R1 layers a deeper Research Patronage venue at Axiom Labs alongside the existing investment card; both are visible in the station hub. The two systems are conceptually adjacent (both involve research and yield); they are mechanically separate.

#### SA-R2 — Dr. Okafor's Legacy Narrative Arc

**Status**: done
**Phase**: Phase IV | **Size**: M | **Effort**: 1 week
**Depends on**: SA-R1 | **Blocks**: SA-R3

**Goal.** Author the long-running ethics-in-research thread that Dr. Nadia Kweon carries on top of SA-R1's project-patronage venue. Reveal the arc across project completions (not visit count) by tagging each of the 10 SA-R1 project templates as `heal` / `profit` / `neutral`-aligned and tracking running heal-vs-profit completion counts in `OkaforResearchState`. Six gated Kweon dialogue beats surface in `OkaforView` over the player's funding history (first-heal, first-profit, heal-pattern at 3, profit-pattern at 3, heal-ending at +5 spread, profit-ending at +5 spread). One optional Kweon-offered mission triggers off the heal-pattern beat and routes through the standard mission system. Founder's principle ("Knowledge that does not heal is knowledge wasted." — `character_voices.md:516`) is the central line the arc bends around. No new NPCs; no new view; no new mechanics — pure narrative extension on existing SA-R1 surface.

**Acceptance criteria.**
1. `OKAFOR_PROJECT_ETHICS` module-level dict in `spacegame/models/okafor_research.py` covers all 10 project ids exactly. Tally is 3 heal / 4 profit / 3 neutral per Decision 2. A test asserts the keyset equals the keyset of `OKAFOR_PROJECT_TEMPLATES` and that every value is one of `"heal" | "profit" | "neutral"`.
2. `OkaforResearchState` has three new fields — `legacy_heal_completed: int = 0`, `legacy_profit_completed: int = 0`, `legacy_ending: str = ""` — that round-trip through `to_dict` / `from_dict`. A legacy-save fixture without these keys loads with the documented defaults; no exception, no warning.
3. `_tick_okafor_projects` increments the right counter on the success branch only (failures do not move ethics counters): a heal-tagged project's success bumps `legacy_heal_completed`; a profit-tagged project's success bumps `legacy_profit_completed`; a neutral-tagged project's success bumps neither. Verified by a parametrized test that funds and ticks one of each kind and asserts the resulting counters.
4. `pending_legacy_beat(state, dialogue_flags)` returns dialogue ids in this priority (Decision 4): if `legacy_ending` is non-empty, return None (arc terminal); else if `heal_completed - profit_completed >= 5` AND `heal_completed >= 6` AND `okafor_legacy_heal_ending_seen` is unset, return `"kweon_legacy_heal_ending"`; else the same for profit; else if `heal_completed >= 3` AND the heal-pattern flag is unset, return `"kweon_legacy_heal_pattern"`; else the same for profit; else if `heal_completed >= 1` AND the first-heal flag is unset, return `"kweon_legacy_first_heal"`; else the same for profit; else None. Each branch verified by direct unit test.
5. `OkaforView._kweon_dialogue_id()` routes in this exact order: failure_debrief_pending → `kweon_failure_debrief`; else `pending_legacy_beat` is non-None → that tree id; else `kweon_okafor_intro`. Three tests cover the three routing paths.
6. Closing an arc-beat tree sets the matching `okafor_legacy_<beat>_seen` flag exactly once. A test funds + ticks the heal-pattern threshold, opens Kweon, dismisses the tree, and asserts `okafor_legacy_heal_pattern_seen` is True. Re-opening Kweon then surfaces the next pending beat (or ambient).
7. Reaching the heal-ending or profit-ending tree's terminal node sets `OkaforResearchState.legacy_ending` to `"heal"` or `"profit"` respectively. After the ending fires, `pending_legacy_beat` returns None and Kweon's button reverts to ambient. Verified by both endings' scenario test.
8. The optional mission `okafor_legacy_clinic_run` is gated on `required_flags: ["okafor_legacy_heal_pattern_seen"]`. The mission file loads through `DataLoader.load_missions` (verified by a parser test). The mission's reward chain bumps `kweon_relationship_value` by 1 (clamped at the SA-R1 cap of 10) and sets `okafor_legacy_mission_completed`.
9. 4 new journal entries fire on their respective trigger flags (`okafor_legacy_first_heal_seen`, `okafor_legacy_first_profit_seen`, `okafor_legacy_heal_ending_seen`, `okafor_legacy_profit_ending_seen`). Each entry passes the Writing Bible scanner. Each entry's `system_id` is `axiom_labs`. Triggers are deduped by the journal manager (no entry refires).
10. Voice check: every authored line in the 6 dialogue trees, the mission file's `description` and `hint`, and the 4 journal entries passes the Writing Bible scanner (zero em-dashes, zero `couldn't help but`, zero `a testament to`, zero `no X, no Y` parallel-negation, zero banned NPC names). **Risks / open questions.**
- ~~Ethics-tag storage location.~~ **LOCKED** (Decision 1): a module-level `OKAFOR_PROJECT_ETHICS: dict[str, str]` lookup in `okafor_research.py`, NOT a new field on the frozen `OkaforProjectTemplate` dataclass. *Rationale*: SA-R1 ships 10 frozen templates; adding a defaulted field is technically non-breaking but bloats the template schema for a downstream-only concern. A separate lookup table is single-purpose, single-grep-target, and lets the categorization shift in SA-R3 polish without re-touching SA-R1's content tables. Test surface: `test_okafor_research.py` asserts the keyset equals the template keyset and every value is one of the three legal strings.
- ~~Project ethics categorization.~~ **LOCKED** (Decision 2): 3 heal / 4 profit / 3 neutral. Heal: `low_meta_analysis_pediatric`, `mid_field_clinic_supply_chain`, `high_post_outbreak_vaccine_synthesis`. Profit: `low_industrial_dust_filtration`, `mid_orbital_propulsion_efficiency`, `mid_alloy_corrosion_mining_belt`, `high_quantum_sensor_capstone`. Neutral: `low_protein_folding_replication`, `low_archive_recovery`, `mid_neural_synthesis_protocol`. *Rationale*: heal projects directly serve clinical / public-health outcomes per the founder's principle ("knowledge that does not heal is knowledge wasted"). Profit projects serve industrial / commercial / sensor-network outcomes that pay well but do not heal. Neutral projects are basic-science work that does not cleanly belong to either side. The 3/4/3 split lets the player reach either ending in 6+ completions across about 8-12 visits, which fits the vision's "5-8 visits or specific project completions" cadence.
- ~~Beat count and arc structure.~~ **LOCKED** (Decision 3): 6 beats — first-heal, first-profit, heal-pattern (3 completions), profit-pattern (3 completions), heal-ending (+5 spread, 6+ heals), profit-ending (+5 spread, 6+ profits). *Rationale*: vision says "multi-step storyline that surfaces over many visits" — 6 beats split symmetrically gives Kweon room to develop the institutional-fatigue → founder's-principle → ending arc on either side without the player feeling the script is on rails. Pattern beats name Dr. Okafor explicitly for the first time, which matches the voice sheet's "founder's words quoted only when she needs the authority she does not personally feel" — by the time the player has shown 3 completions on one side, the question of alignment is real enough to require borrowed authority.
- ~~Beat priority order.~~ **LOCKED** (Decision 4): endings > patterns > firsts; within each tier, the side whose counter is larger fires first; if tied, heal fires first (the founder's principle is the institution's stated north star, and the arc bends toward it absent contrary evidence). *Rationale*: priority order matters when the player crosses two thresholds in one tick (e.g., funds two projects simultaneously). Endings before patterns is correct because once the spread is reached, the pattern beat is no longer load-bearing; firing it after the ending would be backwards. Heal-tied-with-profit defaulting to heal is a small editorial choice — the institutional voice quotes the founder's principle without irony when the player has shown any heal commitment.
- ~~Journal-entry count and voice register.~~ **LOCKED** (Decision 5): 4 new entries — first-heal, first-profit, heal-ending, profit-ending — in `data/journal/entries.json`. NOT in a separate `data/journal/research.json` file (the journal manager loads exactly one file per `data_loader.py:1864`). Pattern beats DO NOT get journal entries; they are dialogue-only beats. *Rationale*: pattern beats are mid-arc connective tissue that lives in dialogue; journal entries are reserved for the moments the player will want to look back at. Endings are the load-bearing player-record beats. Voice register: player's matter-of-fact log voice for the body, one Kweon-quoted line per entry as anchor. Each entry's `system_id` is `axiom_labs`.
- ~~Optional mission scope.~~ **LOCKED** (Decision 6): one mission, heal-side only, gated on `okafor_legacy_heal_pattern_seen`. The mission asks the player to deliver an existing commodity (`medical_supplies`) to an existing frontier-aligned system Kweon names in the pattern beat. Reward chain: +1 `kweon_relationship_value`, set `okafor_legacy_mission_completed`, credits payout. *Rationale*: vision says "optional mission triggered by funding ethically-loaded research" (singular). One mission keeps authoring scope inside the M-sized week, matches the SA-2 pilgrimage / SA-V investment-intro pattern (one mission file per arc), and tests the gating-via-arc-beat-flag pattern that SA-X1 will lean on. A profit-side mission is NOT authored; profit-aligned narrative pays in credits and faction reputation through SA-R1's existing project rewards, which is correct for the institution-keeps-running register.
- ~~`okafor_collaborator_share` flag consumers.~~ **LOCKED — OUT OF SCOPE for SA-R2** (Decision 7): SA-R1 registered eight `okafor_collaborator_share_<researcher_id>` flags (one per researcher × project) as KNOWN_PRODUCER_ONLY_ORPHANS, with the comment that SA-R2 would wire consumers. SA-R2 does NOT wire those consumers. *Rationale*: those flags surface team-fund-collaboration history, which is a different narrative axis (which Institute staff has the player worked with) than the heal/profit ethics axis SA-R2 commits to. Splicing both into one sprint risks scope bloat and tonal incoherence — the Kweon arc lives or dies on the founder's principle, not on collaborator history. Either SA-R3 (polish) picks up consumer wiring, or a follow-up SA-R2-FOLLOW-1 is opened. The producer-only orphans stay registered; the SI-3 scanner remains clean. Flag this in the SA-R2 review's "follow-ups noted" block.
- ~~Polish fold-in scope.~~ **LOCKED** (Decision 8): save/load round-trip, voice-check pass, scenario test fold IN. Crew banter on legacy-ending (defer to SA-X6), achievement unlocks for either ending (defer to SA-X7), cross-anchor narrative threading e.g. Wreckers' Guild reaction to the heal-ending (defer to SA-X1), audio identity per ending (defer to SA-X9), tutorial-pass refinement (defer to SA-X3), polish + tuning (defer to SA-R3) all stay in their downstream sprints. *Rationale*: same calculus as SA-R1 — the three folds are the minimum bar for the arc to feel finished; everything else is the explicit deliverable of a downstream sprint that already names SA-R2 as a dependency.

#### SA-R3 — Research Patronage polish

**Status**: done
**Phase**: Phase IV | **Size**: S | **Effort**: 3-5 days
**Depends on**: SA-R1, SA-R2 | **Blocks**: SA-X1, SA-X2, SA-X4, SA-X5, SA-X6, SA-X7, SA-X9

**Goal.** Finish-the-feature polish + tuning pass over the SA-R1 / SA-R2 Research Patronage chain. Six concrete pieces of work: (1) author a Research Patronage tuning report capturing the per-template numeric audit, the royalty / lump-sum break-even math, and the locked balance baseline; (2) replace the flat 30% failure-refund constant with a tier-aware refund table (low 0.50 / mid 0.30 / high 0.20) so high-risk projects sting more on loss and low-risk projects refund a larger share when their rare 5% failure fires; (3) ship a template numeric-audit data-validation test enforcing locked ranges across all 10 SA-R1 templates so future template additions inherit the validation; (4) close SA-R2-FOLLOW-1 by adding a `kweon_relationship` mission reward type and wiring it into the existing `okafor_legacy_clinic_run` mission so SA-R2 AC #8 ("bumps `kweon_relationship_value` by 1") is no longer a pre-authorized stopgap; (5) close SA-R2's deferred consumer for `okafor_legacy_mission_completed` by authoring one short Kweon callback dialogue tree (`kweon_legacy_post_clinic_run`) that fires once after the clinic-run mission completes and routes through the existing `_kweon_dialogue_id()` priority chain; (6) close SA-R1-FOLLOW-2 by replacing the auto-picked `["dr_iris_navarro"]` collaborator stub in `OkaforView._handle_event` with a real picker UI (3 researcher checkboxes + Nuri-when-crewed checkbox; cap at 2; live cost / duration math; Confirm / Cancel) so the locked 1.5×-cost-per-collaborator / 0.7-duration-per-collaborator math is reachable for all collaborator combinations rather than only the 1-collaborator Iris path.
